bibl.title: The Authority of Orpheus, Poet and Bard: Between Tradition and Written Practice.
bibl.seg: Claude Calame, The Authority of Orpheus, Poet and Bard: Between Tradition and Written Practice.

Phillip Mitsis & Christos Tsagalis (edd.), Allusion, Authority, and Truth. Critical Perspectives on Greek Poetic and Rhetorical Praxis = Trends in Classics. Supplementary Volumes. 7 (Berlin - New York, 2010) pp. 13-35.
bibl.note: Orpheus as poet-musician and as master of initiation. - Orpheus and cosmo-theogony in epic diction. - Between "narrative" and "speech": Homeric diction. - Procedures of poetic enunciation. - Hermeneutic and initiatory erudition in an Orphic commentary [P. Derveni (= MP3 2465.1; LDAB 7049)]. - Commentary and the authority of the poem. - Interpretative procedures reserved for the initiated. - Between physical principles and divine forces. - The initiatory itinerary of a written hermeneutic practice. - Orpheus and the authority of written-oral text.
